penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: ETL pipeline setup and configuration for ODBC-source environments requires per-customer engineering work to map schemas, test sync jobs, handle edge cases — not automatable by Claude alone.

penalties_applied.name: requires_synchronous_human
penalties_applied.reason: Selling a data infrastructure replacement to IT managers at mid-market companies realistically requires discovery calls and scoping conversations before any deal closes.

rationale: The buyer is real — an IT manager at a subsidiary company with a genuine production need and implied budget — and they're already in purchase mode replacing EOL software, which is a meaningful willingness-to-pay signal. However, building an actual ETL product that handles ODBC sources, schema mapping, incremental sync, and failure recovery requires substantial custom infrastructure engineering far beyond Claude prompts and a Stripe link, scoring it very low on buildability. More critically, every customer deployment is bespoke, making autonomous delivery impossible and requiring human engineering involvement per engagement. This is a legitimate B2B problem but the wrong shape for a solo non-technical Claude factory.
solution_plan: This is not viable for this factory. An ODBC-based ETL service is a software infrastructure product that requires database drivers, connection management, schema introspection, and per-customer configuration — none of which Claude can build or operate autonomously. A solo non-technical operator could not build, sell, or maintain this without hiring engineers. Consider passing this signal to a developer-focused acquirer or filing it as market validation for a future pivot, but do not invest further now.
notes: Fails buildability_with_ai (3 < 6 floor) and operational_autonomy (3 < 7 floor) build gates. Penalties bring total well below validate threshold. Drop.
